detailed_description:
Photoreal cinematic live-action, 1881 London, 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:04. The shot begins from <Picture 2>: a wide from the street side: the brick front of Number 3 rising across the whole TOP of frame with three tiers of blank curtainless windows, the yellow clay path running up the CENTRE to the front door, the three-foot brick wall and its wooden rails crossing the BOTTOM of frame. The camera is on the street pavement outside the wooden rails, at a standing man's eye height, square on to the house front, a 35mm lens turned up the clay path. The three-foot brick wall and its rails cross the BOTTOM of frame. The camera pushes in a hand's breadth up the path toward the door as the fog drifts a hand's breadth across the house front, from 00:00 to 00:04. Behind him one stalwart police constable in a tall helmet leaning against the brick wall, and five or six loafers in caps craning over the rails behind him, from 00:00 to 00:04.
[Shot 2] From 00:04 to 00:08. At 00:04 the shot cuts to an insert on one blank first-floor window of Number 3, beginning from <Picture 3>: a yellowed card standing in the corner of the pane with the two words "TO LET" in heavy black block capitals across it, the fog lying grey on the glass; only what <Picture 3> shows is in frame. The camera is on the clay path inside the rails, angled up at the first floor, a 100mm lens turned on the one blank window. The fog lies grey between the lens and the glass. At the first frame One blank curtainless window of the first floor fills the frame, its black-painted sash weathered, its brickwork wet, a yellowed card standing in the corner of the lower pane, the two words "TO LET" standing in heavy black wood-type block capitals across its foxed buff face, the glass grey with fog. The camera pushes in a hand's breadth on the words "TO LET" as the fog thickens across the pane by a hand's breadth, from 00:04 to 00:08.

overall_soundscape: The ambience of the front garden of Number 3 Lauriston Gardens runs under the whole take: its own air, the surfaces underfoot and the fabric of the place around it. Cloth, boots, wood and glass carry the physical action, and the movement and low murmur of the people at work nearby carry under it throughout.
